    >How the forecast is builtPhysics law stretched by an acceleration factor, plus a bounded neural correctionShow
    

      
The encoder reads up to 24 tokens from the revealed history (age, health, health change, charge-time drifts) and emits the unit's physics parameters: initial health, wear rate and exponent, knee position and sharpness. With zero history it falls back to the learned population curve for NCM, stretched in time by the Arrhenius and C-rate acceleration factor for 25 °C and this cell's protocol.

      
H(τ) = H₀ − a·τₑz − knee(τₑ) + δ(τₑ), with τₑ = AF·τ. The correction δ is capped at ±0.06 health and vanishes at age zero, so a short history cannot pull the forecast away from the physics. P(failed) is a sigmoid around the 0.80 line whose spread grows with forecast distance.

      
Forecasts on this page were produced by the trained checkpoints on the actual XJTU measurement files, at every 10-cycle horizon from 0 to 200. Nothing is fitted to the hidden future. Effective C-rates for XJTU are protocol averages, as in the training pipeline.

    

  




Public research dataset (XJTU, via PINN4SOH). Held-out cells; no customer data. Forecast values are model output, not measurements.
